'''Héctor Melesio Cuén Ojeda'''{{Family name footnote|Cuén|[[Ojeda (surname)|Ojeda]]|lang=Mexican}} (October 25, 1955 – July 25, 2024) was a Mexican chemist, pharmacist, biologist, and politician. He was a [[Rector (academia)|rector]] of the [[Autonomous University of Sinaloa]] from 2005 to 2009 and [[municipal president]] of [[Culiacán]], [[Sinaloa]], between January 2011 and February 2012. In July 2024 he was shot dead in his vehicle in [[Culiacán]].

==Life and career==
Cuén Ojeda was born on October 25, 1955, in [[Badiraguato]], [[Sinaloa]], [[Mexico]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Dr. Héctor Melesio Cuén Ojeda |url=http://i.esmas.com/documento/0/000/002/013/DR_HECTOR_MELESIO_CUEN_OJEDA.doc |work=Esmas |accessdate=18 September 2009 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110727081808/http://i.esmas.com/documento/0/000/002/013/DR_HECTOR_MELESIO_CUEN_OJEDA.doc |archivedate=27 July 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He studied at the [[Autonomous University of Sinaloa]], where he earned a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]]. After graduating from the university, he returned and was its rector from 2005 to 2009. From 2011 to 2012, he was the [[municipal president of Culiacán]] and, from 2013 to 2016, he sat in the [[Congress of Sinaloa]].<ref name=quien>{{cite news |last1=Castillo |first1=Juan |title=Quién era Héctor Melesio Cuén, el hombre cuyo homicidio destapó el presunto vínculo del Mayo Zambada con Rocha Moya |url=https://www.infobae.com/mexico/2026/05/12/quien-era-hector-melesio-cuen-el-hombre-cuyo-homicidio-destapo-el-presunto-vinculo-del-mayo-zambada-con-rocha-moya/ |work=[[Infobae]] |date=12 May 2026 |lang=es}}</ref>

He was elected to the [[Chamber of Deputies (Mexico)|Chamber of Deputies]] from the [[Institutional Revolutionary Party]]'s proportional representation list for the [[Electoral regions of Mexico|first electoral region]] in the [[2024 Mexican general election|June 2024 general election]].<ref name="univ"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Héctor Melesio Cuén Ojeda |url=https://candidaturas.ine.mx/detalleCandidato/11345/5 |website=Candidatas y candidatos, conóceles |publisher=[[Instituto Nacional Electoral]] |access-date=13 August 2024}}</ref>

== Assassination ==
{{See also|Capture of El Mayo}}
Cuén Ojeda was killed on July 25, 2024. He was 68.<ref name="univ">{{cite web|url=https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/estados/muere-hector-melesio-cuen-diputado-federal-electo-de-fuerza-y-corazon-por-mexico-tras-herida-de-bala/|title=Muere Héctor Melesio Cuén, diputado federal electo de Fuerza y Corazón por México, tras herida de bala|work=El Universal|date=25 July 2024|language=Spanish}}</ref> 

Initial reports of the crime published by the attorney-general of Sinaloa stated he had been shot in his vehicle at a filling station near Culiacán, but later claims maintained he was murdered at a ranch where he had been lured to attend a meeting with drug trafficker [[Ismael Zambada]] to settle his disputes with Governor [[Rubén Rocha Moya]]; blood samples located there by the federal [[Attorney General of Mexico|attorney-general's office]] (FGR) appeared to confirm that version.<ref name=quien/> 

On 11 August 2024 the federal attorney-general's office announced it was investigating a possible connection between Cuén Ojeda's murder and the [[Sinaloa]] [[Illegal drug trade|drug-traffickers]] Ismael Zambada and [[Joaquín Guzmán López]], who were taken into custody in the [[United States]] later that day in circumstances that remain unclear.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Evair Saldaña |first1=Iván |title=Investiga FGR relación de asesinato del ex rector con 'El Mayo' y Joaquín Guzmán |url=https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2024/08/11/politica/investiga-fgr-si-asesinato-del-ex-rector-implica-a-2018el-mayo2019-y-joaquin-guzman-647 |access-date=12 August 2024 |work=La Jornada |date=11 August 2024}}</ref>

Sinaloa Attorney-General [[Sara Bruna Quiñónez Estrada]] resigned on 16 August 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-08-16 |title=¿Quién es Sara Bruna?: fiscal de Sinaloa que renunció por caso Cuén |url=https://www.milenio.com/politica/sara-bruna-fiscal-sinaloa-renuncio-caso-cuen |access-date=2026-05-03 |website=Grupo Milenio |language=es}}</ref>
